License Agreement Request

A complete, process walkthrough of the project-specific License Agreement Request (LAR) in the NYC HPD PIMS system — from the Development Team’s submission on the external portal through HPD’s internal review, approvals, and final verification.

This guide is written for people who are new to both Salesforce and the License Agreement process. It follows one request end to end so you can see what each screen does and what to expect next.

Tip: click any screenshot to enlarge it for a closer look.

About This Guide

A License Agreement gives a Development Team temporary access to a site (for example, to perform geotechnical borings, environmental testing, or install scaffolding/fencing). There are two types of License Agreement Request:

  • Project-specific — tied to an existing HPD project.
  • General — not linked to any project.

A developer can start a request from three different places.

  • License Agreement Requests tab — the tab at the top of the portal.
  • My Requests area — the developer’s own list of requests.
  • From within a specific project — creates a project-specific request that is automatically linked to that project.

This guide covers the project-specific type and starts the request from a specific project.

Login is not covered here. Each part of the guide begins from the screen you see immediately after signing in.

Purpose of This Guide

This document is a hands-on training reference for the project-specific License Agreement Request. Each step pairs an actual application screenshot with a clear Action (what to do) and Result (what to expect). Where helpful, steps also reference the corresponding step in the Visio future-state process flow for traceability.

Who Should Use This Guide

  • Development Team / applicants who submit License Agreement Requests on the external portal.
  • HPD staff who review and process requests — PM Directors, Land Use Coordinators, LUP Executive Directors, LUP Deputy Directors, LUP reviewers, Project Managers, Legal Support, Owners, and other related specialist approvers.
  • New PIMS / Salesforce users who need a guided, plain-language introduction.

Before You Begin

  • A valid PIMS account with the appropriate permissions (external portal access for applicants, the relevant role/queue for HPD staff).
  • For a project-specific request, the project must already exist in PIMS.
  • The required documents and insurance ready to upload — the exact list depends on the scope you select.
  • A supported web browser (latest Google Chrome recommended) and a stable connection.

Process at a Glance

The project-specific License Agreement Request follows this overall path:

  • 1Developer submits the request from a specific project (external portal)
  • 2HPD intake & eligibility review
  • 3Submit for approval — LUP / Land Use Coordinator guidance
  • 4PM Director review
  • 5Project Manager prepares & submits the package
  • 6Specialist approvals (condensed)
  • 7Legal Support uploads the Final License Agreement
  • 8Land Use Coordinator final review
  • 9Owner review & document verification
  • 10Signature (DocuSign) — agreement in effect

Part A — The External PIMS Portal (Development Team)

A project-specific License Agreement Request is submitted by the Development Team on the external PIMS Portal. This guide starts the request from inside a specific project (see the note above for the other two starting points). After signing in, follow the steps below.

Step 1: Navigate to the Specific Project

Action Sign in to the PIMS Portal and open the specific project you need site access for.

Result The project opens to its Project Information page. Because the request is started from inside a project, it will be created as a project-specific License Agreement Request and automatically linked to this project. Only the project details page opens, where you can see all the project-related details and information for reference, and you can track the project status from here.

Step 2: Add a New Request

Action On the project page, go to the My Requests tab and click Add New.

Result PIMS opens the request-type selection screen, where you choose which kind of request to start for this project.

Step 3: Choose License Agreement Request

Action Several request types can be initiated here. Under License Agreement Request, click Complete Form.

Result The New License Agreement Request form opens.

Step 4: Complete the License Agreement Request Form

Action Complete the form. The Project Name is already filled in and cannot be edited because the request was started from a specific project. Complete the Scope field — this is a multi-select field that determines both the direction of the approval process and which documents are required. Fill in all remaining required and relevant fields, then click Add Insurance.

Result The form captures the site and scope details. Based on the selected scope, the system flags additional requirements — for example, a Pollution Insurance is required reminder appears — and the document checklist (shown later) is generated to match the scope.

Step 5: Add Insurance Details

Action In the insurance pop-up, type the Insurance Type and select the Insurance Expiration Date, then click Save.

Result The insurance policy is added to the request and appears as a row in the Insurance Details list. You can add multiple insurance policies as needed by clicking the Add Insurance button again.

Step 6: Continue to Documents

Action Once you have added all required insurance policies, click Next.

Result PIMS advances to the document upload step for this request.

Step 7: Review the Scope-Based Document Checklist

Action Review the Document Checklist, which is generated based on the scope you selected. These are the documents the Development Team must upload before submission. Click the upload action on a document line.

Result All listed documents are required — the system will not move forward and shows an error if any required document is missing.

Step 8: Upload the Required Documents

Action Choose the relevant document(s) from your local folder and upload. The system allows multiple documents under a single document line, so you can add more than one file where needed.

Result Each uploaded file is attached to its document line, and the line’s status updates from pending.

Step 9: Submit the Request

Action Once all required documents are uploaded, click Submit.

Result The new License Agreement Request is submitted from the external portal to HPD. PIMS confirms the application was submitted successfully and displays its application number (for example BLA-0000000513).

Step 10: Confirmation and Application Number

Action Read the confirmation message and note your application number. From here you can return to the portal Home page or open the View Application Page. Click View Application Page to review the new request.

Result You are navigated to the newly created License Agreement Request record page, where you can see all the details.

Step 11: Review the Submitted Request

Action Review the submitted request.

Result You can see all the submitted details along with tabs for Documents, Actions, and Message Board. At the bottom, the Insurance Information section lists all the insurance that was uploaded.

Part B — The Internal PIMS Application (HPD Staff)

Once submitted, the request is processed by HPD staff in the internal PIMS application (Salesforce). As the request moves through the approval chain, the logged-in user and the record’s status change to reflect who is currently responsible. Several intermediate specialist-approval stages are largely repetitive and have been condensed here so the guide stays focused on the overall path.

Step 12: Open the HPD Staff Home

Action Sign in to the internal PIMS application. This is the Home tab. Click the dropdown (arrow) menu beside Home, which opens the list of objects.

Result The Home page shows your Action Items, Active Modules, and Pending Milestones in My Queue — everything you need to track in one place. Clicking the dropdown beside Home opens the list of objects available in the PIMS portal, which you can navigate to from here. Note: this area is still under progress and may change based on the process.

Step 13: Select License Applications

Action From the list of objects (Projects, Cases, Applications, Accounts, Contacts, and more), select License Applications.

Result The License Applications object opens.

Step 14: Open the License Agreement Request List View

Action License Applications offers several list views. From the list view selector at the top (it opens on Recently Viewed), click the arrow and open the License Agreement Request list view.

Result The list view shows all License Agreement Requests submitted from the external portal.

Step 15: Sort, Filter, and Open a Record

Action Use the filter and sort options at the top-right to narrow the list. Salesforce also supports inline column sorting — click a column header such as Application ID, Project, Created Date, or Last Updated to sort. Click any application to open its record.

Result The selected License Agreement Request record opens.

Step 16: Review the Application and Begin Processing

Action Review the details submitted by the developer. The highlight panel at the top shows the record’s most important information, and the status path tracks where the record stands. Use the tabs — for example Insurance Information (all insurance details) and Documents (all uploaded documents). On the right, the Activity panel shows the task created for the PM Director (created whenever an application is submitted), and Guidance for Success explains the workflow. When ready, click Mark Application Status as Complete.

Result The record is now in review and ready for the eligibility decision.

Process map reference: Visio future-state flow, Step 1 (project-specific).

Step 17: Set “Is Request Eligible”

Action Once the status is updated, the Is Request Eligible field appears, with guidance on what to do. Click the pencil icon to edit and select the appropriate value — here, Yes. (Selecting No sends the request down a different path; refer to the Visio future-state flow for that branch.)

Result The eligibility determination is recorded on the request.

Process map reference: Visio future-state flow, Step 2 (project-specific).

Step 18: Save the Eligibility Decision

Action Click Save.

Result The Is Request Eligible value is saved to the record.

Step 19: Submit for Approval

Action Once the field is updated, the Submit for Approval button appears at the top. Here the PM Director submits the record to the LUP Executive Director / LUP Deputy Director / Land Use Coordinator for guidance on whether the request is eligible. Click Submit for Approval.

Result The approval submission window opens.

Step 20: Add Review Comments and Submit

Action Add appropriate comments to help the reviewer understand the submission, then submit it.

Result The request is routed to the LUP Executive Director / LUP Deputy Director / Land Use Coordinator for review.

Process map reference: Visio future-state flow, Step 2.1.

Step 21: Track Progress on the Approval Work Item Tab

Action Open the Approval Work Item tab.

Result You can see that the record has been submitted for approval to the LUP Executive Director / LUP Deputy Director / Land Use Coordinator.

Step 22: Reviewer Picks Up the Work Item

Action The assigned reviewer (LUP Executive Director / LUP Deputy Director / Land Use Coordinator) signs in. On their Home page, the action item is assigned to them — click View to open it.

Result The reviewer’s Action Items list shows the work item assigned to them, ready to act on.

Step 23: Reviewer Records the Eligibility Decision

Action The application record opens, where the approver can review all the necessary details, insurance information, and submitted documents. On the left, the Action Item lets the approver Approve or Reject and add decision comments. Click Submit.

Result The reviewer’s decision is recorded and the request advances.

Process map reference: Visio future-state flow, Step 2.2.

Step 24: Routed to the PM Director

Action Once approved, the request goes to the second approval step — the PM Director — to decide whether to reject the application. This also creates a task for the PM Director noting that the application review is completed. Select Yes to reject or No to advance, add a comment, and click Submit.

Result The License Agreement Request is accepted and approved, along with additional guidance. After the PM Director approves, the PM Director assigns the Project Manager (LA Manager); an automatic task is created and the assigned person is notified.

Process map reference: Visio future-state flow, Step 3.

Step 25: Project Manager Reviews the Record

Action The Project Manager (PM) logs in and reviews the record. Review the Guidance for Success shown on the record, then click the Documents tab. If any changes or updates are needed, the PM can reject or request information from the Documents tab, or exchange details on the Message Board.

Result The record shows the Guidance for Success, which explains what the Project Manager needs to do at this stage, and the Documents tab opens, showing the package documents to be prepared.

Step 26: Open the Pending Documents

Action On the Documents tab you can see the pending documents, and you can filter the list using the status selector at the top-right. Upload the required documents.

Result The required package documents are listed with their current status.

Step 27: Confirm the Submitted Documents

Action Once all the documents are uploaded, review the list.

Result The checklist now shows the list of submitted documents.

Step 28: Submit the Package for Approval

Action Once all the documents are submitted and the package is ready, click Submit for Approval.

Result The approval submission window opens for the completed package.

Step 29: Add Package Comments and Submit

Action Add the appropriate comments and click Submit.

Result The completed License Agreement package is routed to the PM Director for review.

Step 30: PM Director Opens the New Action Item

Action On the PM Director’s Home screen, a new action item is added. Click View to open it.

Result The PM Director opens the assigned work item.

Step 31: PM Director Records the Decision

Action The PM Director reviews the application, makes the approval decision, updates the comments, and clicks Submit.

Result The PM Director’s decision is recorded and the package advances through the approval chain.

Step 32: Review the Approval History

Action Open the Approval Work Item tab.

Result You can see the approval history and the next approval that has been submitted.

Step 33: Approvals Complete — Legal Support

Action Continue tracking the request as it completes the approval process.

Result Once the application completes all the approval steps, you can see the full approval history, and the request is now with Legal Support. (The multiple intermediate specialist-approval stages are mostly repetitive and have been omitted here for clarity.)

Step 34: Legal Support Opens the Application

Action When the Legal Support team opens the application, they see the relevant Guidance for Success. Click the Documents tab to upload the Final License Agreement.

Result The Documents tab opens, ready for the Final License Agreement.

Step 35: Upload the Final License Agreement

Action Upload the Final License Agreement document.

Result The Final License Agreement is attached to the request.

Step 36: Confirm the Final Document

Action On the right, in the Action Item, the Legal Support team selects Yes, adds the appropriate comments, and clicks Next.

Result The Final License Agreement is confirmed as uploaded, and the request advances.

Step 37: Land Use Coordinator Final Review

Action The request is sent to the Land Use Coordinator for review of the License Agreement. The reviewer clicks Approve, adds comments, and clicks Submit.

Result The Land Use Coordinator’s approval is recorded and the request advances.

Step 38: Owner Review and Verification

Action Once approved, the request automatically goes to the Owner of the application to review and verify it. Review the Guidance for Success and click the Documents tab.

Result The Documents tab opens so the Owner can review and verify the final document.

Step 39: Review and Verify the Document

Action Review the document and Verify it.

Result Verifying the Final License Agreement confirms it is correct and ready to proceed to signature (the DocuSign signing and countersignature steps follow).

Summary

In this guide you followed a project-specific License Agreement Request from start to finish. On the external portal, the Development Team started the request from a specific project, completed the scope-driven form, recorded insurance, uploaded the required documents, and submitted — receiving an application number. In the internal application, HPD staff reviewed the request, recorded eligibility, and routed it for approval to the LUP / Land Use Coordinator. After that decision, the request moved to the PM Director, the Project Manager prepared and submitted the License Agreement package, and it passed through the approval chain. Legal Support uploaded the Final License Agreement, the Land Use Coordinator gave final review, and the Owner reviewed and verified the document — after which it proceeds to signature via DocuSign and the agreement takes effect.

Notes & Disclaimers

  • This guide covers the project-specific License Agreement workflow only; the general (non-project) workflow differs at the intake and assignment steps.
  • The exact approval stages depend on the request’s scope (e.g. environmental testing, geotechnical borings, scaffolding/fencing, soil characterization). Several repetitive specialist-approval stages are condensed in this guide.
  • For decision branches (for example, when Is Request Eligible is set to No), refer to the Visio future-state process flow.
  • Screens, field names, and buttons may vary by role, permissions, browser, resolution, and future PIMS updates.
  • Names, application numbers, and data shown are from a training/sandbox environment and are for illustration only.
